question: How do initial C-H bond cleavages influence the formation of radicals and subsequent products in JP-10 pyrolysis?
answer: Initial C-H bond cleavages in JP-10 pyrolysis play a critical role in radical formation and subsequent product distribution. Theoretical calculations at 1500 K predict that C-H bond scission leads to key radicals such as allyl (C3H5) and cyclopentenyl (C5H7), which further decompose or recombine to form major products like ethylene (C2H4), cyclopentadiene (C5H6), and allene (C3H4). The yield of these radicals and products is temperature-dependent, with C2 and C4 group products increasing at higher temperatures, while C5 species remain dominant. Discrepancies between theory and experiment suggest secondary reactions, such as H-assisted pathways or radical recombination, may influence product distributions, particularly for fulvene (C6H6) and cyclopentenyl radical stability. These findings highlight the importance of C-H bond cleavage in initiating JP-10 decomposition and shaping its pyrolytic product profile.

The paper aims to investigate the pyrolysis mechanisms of exo-tetrahydrodicyclopentadiene (JP-10) under combustion-relevant conditions by performing theoretical calculations of rate constants and product branching ratios. The results are compared with experimental data from molecular beam photoionization mass spectrometry to assess the decomposition pathways and identify key products and trends under varying temperature and pressure conditions. The findings are intended to improve kinetic models for JP-10 pyrolysis.
